doc.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Role models and not just copying
summary: Jazz must be wanted to be learned; start with a role model but find your own voice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I think the same thing holds true with jazz. You could try to teach it but you can’t learn it unless you want to, I mean, you have to like something that you hear and say “sheez, I’d like to do that, I want to play like that.” And it will get you started. And then you get your own thing going. You do what you’re feeling. It comes to you and you can’t go wrong copying somebody else. That’s the mistake a lot of guys make. They want to play like Benny Goodman, they wind up playing like Benny Goodman and they don’t have anything to say of their own. It goes for any instrument, you know. But you have to start someplace.
So, it’s good to have someone to at least be interested in.
Sure. A role model, is that what they call it? Yeah. It’s a good thing, I think. I don’t know how else you can get started.
